newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - T-bond vols edge up on rate hike worries.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - T-bond vols edge up on rate hike worries.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond options crept up in hectic trade as the bond market dipped on concerns over a rate hike at the May 20 Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, dealers said.
Implied volatilities for July and September T-bond futures options on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) rose about a tenth of a point each to 8.9 and 9.0 percent respectively.
"Volatility is picking up," said Brad Tyl, CBOT floor manager for Aubrey G Lanston. "It has been building up for a couple of days as we ready for FOMC."

June T-bond futures, after rising to fresh 2-1/2 month high of 110-22/32 early and then shedding those gains, slid further in the afternoon to a low of 109-24/32 on a news story quoting sources close to the Federal Reserve as saying odds favored a 25-basis point tightening at the FOMC meeting.
Traders said that Richmond Fed president Alfred Broaddus's comments that came out at about the same time also weighed on bonds. Broaddus said the Fed must stay ahead of the the inflation curve.
"This is very important because it sets a whole new tone," Tyl said.
He said the comments today were in quite a contrast to Fed chairman Alan Greenspan's speech last Thursday, which the market perceived to be much softer.
"We were trading at 108-18/32 to 108-20/32 at that time (when Greenspan spoke) and Mr Broaddus and the Reuters story came out at 110-4/32," Tyl noted. "Here's our narrow band. We'll see who wins."
A second CBOT trader said the June futures had been overbought and a correction was overdue anyway.
"I don't see volatilities jumping higher unless we see a more scary move," he said.
Traders said there seemed to be little interest in rolling over June option positions into July or September, even though June contracts expire on Friday and would not cover the FOMC meeting.
According to the CBOT, open interest in June options fell by 4,131 contracts on Monday to 318,212, while that in July options rose by 7,705 to 36,995.

Traders said July options, which have the shortest days-to-maturity among options covering the FOMC meeting, were likely to be well bid this week as traders usually disliked being short gamma prior to an important event like FOMC.
Implied volatilities for Eurodollar futures options on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange were mixed, as they had been for the past few days.
September volatility was a touch lower at around 9.7 percent, while December was up a few tenths at 11.7 percent.
A brokerage trader at the CME said the market had yet to fully price in a quarter-point rate hike and would likely remain cautious and narrow-ranged going into the FOMC meeting.
"We're taking one number at a time," he said, adding that Wednesday's April producer price index and Thursday's consumer prices would be closely scrutinized.
